newsitem.title: USA: Vice presidential candidates attend Al Smith dinner.
newsitem.headline: Vice presidential candidates attend Al Smith dinner.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore and Republican challenger Jack Kemp attended the 51st annual Al Smith Dinner sponsored by the New York Archdiocese on Thursday, filling in for their presidential running mates.
Reports in New York newspapers said President Bill Clinton had not been invited to the dinner, which draws New York's top politicans.

The reports said Cardinal John O'Connor, a strong opponent of abortion, had not invited Clinton because of his veto of a ban on partial-birth abortions. But dinner organisers were cited as saying at the time that Clinton and Republican Bob Dole were not able to attend because of scheduling conflicts.
Asked if he had not invited Clinton or Dole to the dinner, O'Connor said, "Is that what they're saying?"
When a reporter asked, "Is that right?" the cardinal maintained a silence.
The dinner is held in honour of the first Catholic ever to run for president, New York Gov. Al Smith who ran in 1928, losing to Republican Herbert Hoover.
